clue.text: Going too far westward in small county seat

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the county's short name

parts.note: Bucks is the short form of Buckinghamshire

indicators.note: in an across clue westward means read right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means going too far

explanation.surface: Someone overreaching in a little shire's seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is the usual short name of the English county Buckinghamshire. 'Seat' looks like a county town or a seat of power; it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom, the part of the body you sit on, is jokingly called the seat.

clue.text: Sign one's expecting tip for puzzle by Tramp

indicators.note: by means next to, so the tip follows the tramp

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A vagrant gives a hint about a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant woman's belly bump is the visible sign she is expecting a baby.

clue.text: After turning point, there's zero agitation

indicators.note: after places zero behind the turned point
turning means the word for point is spun round to read backwards

parts.note: a dot is a point
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: After a turning point, everything calms down to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or commotion, a state of agitation.

clue.text: Ortega's extremists seizing some power back in capital

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the outer letters wrap round the power unit

parts.note: the outer letters of Ortega, the first and last

indicators.note: back means the power word is read in reverse

parts.note: a watt is a unit, some amount, of power

explanation.surface: The extremes of a Latin American leader seizing power in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Daniel Ortega is Nicaragua's leader; his name's ends, O and A, surround TTAW, which is WATT reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Confined stranger tattoo producer

parts.note: police kettle protesters by penning them in a confined space
rummer is the comparative of rum, odd, so more strange

explanation.surface: A locked-up eccentric who does tattoos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattoo' suggests ink on skin; it is a drumbeat or military display. Kettling is the British police tactic of hemming in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rhythmic drumming, so a timpani player makes one.

clue.text: Graduates with billions to invest love fruitful growth

indicators.note: to invest is to surround or besiege, so the graduates and billions wrap round love

parts.note: two BAs, Bachelors of Arts
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Wealthy graduates putting money into a love affair that bears fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: O (love) sits between the two BAs, with B for billions at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is an African tree bearing large edible fruit, so it is a growth that fruits.

clue.text: Liking Alcott's opening page with description of Little Women

indicators.note: the opening of Alcott's is its first letter

parts.note: petite describes small women

explanation.surface: Fondness for the first page of Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Women' is not the novel but a pun: women who are small are petite.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite is a desire or taste for something, a liking.

clue.text: Holy works of bishop and cleric, one given a sign

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Rev, Reverend, is a cleric
I is the Roman numeral one
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Church books by a bishop and a priest, one marked with a symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Breviaries are books of the daily prayers and readings for the divine office.

clue.text: Shares responsibility to probe British problem

indicators.note: to probe is to poke into, so the responsibility word goes inside

parts.note: an issue is a problem
the onus is the responsibility

explanation.surface: Sharing responsibility for investigating a British difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shares' reads as a verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus issue is a free issue of new stock to existing shareholders.

clue.text: What Buddhist does helps to solve conflicts over time

indicators.note: the conflict-solving word goes over, covering, the time letter, so it sits within

parts.note: a mediator mediates, helping two sides settle a dispute

explanation.surface: A Buddhist peacemaker settling disputes over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: T for time goes inside MEDIATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Meditation is the central contemplative practice of Buddhism.

clue.text: My way to fall foul of the RSPB?

definitions.text: My way to fall foul of the RSPB?

parts.words: My way to fall foul of the RSPB?
parts.note: an exclamation of surprise like My!, which taken literally is pelting birds with rocks

explanation.walkthrough: The RSPB is the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds, a British charity. The answer is an old British cry of astonishment; read literally it attacks birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone the crows is a dated British exclamation of surprise, equivalent to my word.

clue.text: Hymn from nonbeliever after a change of heart

indicators.note: the heart, the central letter, of the nonbeliever's word is swapped for another

parts.note: a pagan is someone outside the main religions, a nonbeliever

explanation.surface: A heathen converts and sings a hymn of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: PAGAN's middle letter G changes to E.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean is a song of praise or triumph, originally to Apollo.

clue.text: Butterflies eat rump steak to start with

parts.note: to swallow is to eat
the rump is the tail end

indicators.note: to start with picks the opening letter of steak

explanation.surface: A dinner instruction: eat the rump steak first.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallowtails are large butterflies named for the tail-like points on their hindwings.

clue.text: Song he composed with firm bass from this person?

indicators.note: composed means put together, arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer writes a song with a strong bass line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bass' points to the low voice in the song; it is the fish, said with a short a.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishmonger sells fish, and bass is a fish you could buy from one.

clue.text: Team's defending shot, ball for Brazilian maestro

indicators.note: defending means guarding, so the team's name surrounds the shot and ball

parts.note: Villa, Aston Villa football club, plus the possessive S
a lob is a high shot in tennis or football
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A football team shields a lofted strike and the ball from a Brazilian.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English football club known as Villa.
explanation.definitionFit: Heitor Villa-Lobos was a Brazilian composer and conductor, the country's best-known classical musician.

clue.text: Is she a bit of a looker?

definitions.text: Is she a bit of a looker?

parts.words: Is she a bit of a looker?
parts.note: a woman's name that is also the coloured part of the eye, a bit of an organ for looking

explanation.walkthrough: 'a looker' sounds like praise for an attractive woman, but here it is an eye, and the woman's name is a part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a female name and also the coloured ring of the eye around the pupil.

clue.text: Adult set out at night, admitting very risky capers?

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the false teeth take in the letter for very

parts.note: false teeth are a set that is taken out at night

explanation.surface: A grown-up sneaks out at night on dangerous escapades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out at night' is not leaving home: it is a set of false teeth, removed at bedtime. V goes inside DENTURES, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventures are exciting, often hazardous exploits, the question mark allowing the loose synonym capers.

clue.text: Impressions made by winsome female going south

indicators.note: going means leaving, so the letter for female drops out

parts.note: fetching means attractive, winsome
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A charming woman leaves an impression as she heads south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going south' looks like one phrase; 'going' deletes the F, and 'south' is S added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints taken from an etched plate, impressions in the printing sense.

clue.text: Misleading words prince's penning daily — pity!

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the prince's name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare, plus the possessive S
FT is the Financial Times, a daily paper
ruth is an old word for pity, surviving in ruthless

explanation.surface: A prince writing deceptive things in the newspaper, which is a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V; the FT is the Financial Times, a British daily, and ruth is an archaic word surviving in ruthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-truths are statements partly true but meant to deceive.

clue.text: School training game in Pacific region

parts.note: PE is physical education, training in school
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Pupils play sport somewhere in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American country with a long Pacific coastline.

clue.text: Area under backbones

indicators.note: in a down clue under means placed below, after the other piece

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A region lying beneath someone's spine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backbones' looks like one word, but it splits into 'back' and the definition 'bones'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterna is the plural of sternum, the breastbone, so these are bones.

clue.text: Awful calamity shook faceless or OK place to live

indicators.note: awful suggests things in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder
faceless means losing the front, the first letter of shook goes

explanation.surface: A disaster shakes up a town that was otherwise a decent place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faceless' takes S off SHOOK to leave HOOK; rearrange that with CALAMITY. 'OK' is the postal code for the US state of Oklahoma.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma City is the capital of Oklahoma, abbreviated OK, so it is an Oklahoman city to live in.

clue.text: Hard to get bitten by green parrot

indicators.note: bitten means held in the teeth, so the green word closes around the letter

parts.note: eco means green, environmentally friendly
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: It is difficult to be bitten by a green parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' looks like the bird; it is the verb, to repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat mechanically, and to echo is to repeat back.

clue.text: Man perhaps gets permission to drop back

indicators.note: the back letter of the phrase is dropped, its last letter going

parts.note: is let means is allowed, gets permission

explanation.surface: A man asks permission to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea; perhaps marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of one.

clue.text: Talk incessantly where French is spoken?

parts.note: to gab is to chatter or talk idly
to go on is to continue without stopping, so ON adds the sense of incessantly

explanation.surface: Someone who never stops talking, especially in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: French is the official language of this country.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a Central African nation, a former French colony whose official language is French.

clue.text: After right wheels, gets fuel supplements for vehicles

indicators.note: after places the wheels and what follows behind the letter for right

parts.note: two round letters O look like a pair of wheels
to frack is to fracture rock to extract gas or oil

explanation.surface: Once the wheels are put on right, a car gets fuelled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' is a picture: the two round letters OO.
explanation.definitionFit: Roof racks are frames fitted on top of cars to carry extra luggage, an add-on to a car.

clue.text: Take paper again around centre for reusing refuse

indicators.note: around means the exam word goes around the next letter

parts.note: to resit is to take an exam paper again

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of reusing

explanation.surface: Recycling instructions: use paper again to cut down on rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a noun meaning rubbish, which suits the recycling picture; it is the verb. S, the centre of REUSING, goes inside RESIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to decline or withstand, close in sense to refusing.

clue.text: Meat left over is stuffed into duck

indicators.note: stuffed into means packed inside, so the two letters go within the duck word

parts.note: to duck is to avoid or escape
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Leftover meat used as stuffing for a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' wants to be the bird being stuffed; it is the verb, escape.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, often veal, beaten flat.
